repo_notes.content: Treat canonical docs, ADRs, configs, tests, and runtime source as source of truth. DeepWiki is a derived navigation surface only and must not contradict AGENTS.md, docs/00-project/ai/memory/README.md, or docs/00-project/ai/memory/agent-memory.md.

pages.title: BioETL Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to BioETL: what it does, who it's for, key features, supported providers, and how the major sections of this wiki relate to each other. Links to child pages for setup and project governance.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for setting up a local development environment: prerequisites, installation via `uv`/`make`, environment variables,  running the first smoke test, and the CLI quick-start. Covers Windows/WSL dual-checkout path.

pages.title: Project Governance and Rules
pages.purpose: Covers RULES.md, ADR index, documentation governance, file-policy, and the project's contribution guidelines. Explains how architectural decisions are recorded and enforced.

pages.title: AI Runtime, Memory, and MCP Governance
pages.purpose: Explains how AI runtime surfaces stay source-first: AGENTS.md, runtime sources in .codex and .gemini, the canonical memory workflow, MCP governance, and DeepWiki as a derived navigation layer. Links to the authoritative memory and validation docs.

page_notes.content: Canonical anchors: AGENTS.md, docs/00-project/ai/memory/README.md, docs/00-project/ai/memory/agent-memory.md, docs/00-project/ai/agents/guides/MEMORY_USAGE.md, src/memory/DAILY_WORKFLOW.md, docs/00-project/ai/agents/policy/POST_CHANGE_VALIDATION.md, docs/00-project/ai/mcp-governance.md, .codex/settings.json, .gemini/settings.json.
DeepWiki is derived navigation only; canonical truth remains in docs, configs, code, tests, and accepted ADRs.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of BioETL's Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) and Medallion data layers. Introduces the five layers (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Composition, Interfaces) and links to child pages for each. Summarises key ADRs.

pages.title: Domain Layer
pages.purpose: Deep dive into the pure domain layer: Ports (Protocol interfaces), Aggregates, Value Objects, Entities, Schemas (Pandera DataFrameModel), Exceptions hierarchy, and the domain's public API facade. Covers domain purity rules and allowed imports.

pages.title: Application Layer
pages.purpose: Covers the orchestration layer: BasePipeline, PipelineRunner, RecordProcessor, BatchExecutor, BaseTransformer, and the data-quality service. Explains how a pipeline run flows from runner to batch to record processing.

pages.title: Infrastructure Layer
pages.purpose: Covers concrete adapters, HTTP client, storage writers, observability implementations, quarantine, locking, and validation. Explains how infrastructure implements domain ports.

pages.title: Composition Layer
pages.purpose: Explains the Dependency Injection wiring layer: factories, provider registry, runtime builders, bootstrap contexts, and how all components are assembled into a runnable pipeline. Covers entrypoints and the composition API.

pages.title: Interfaces Layer
pages.purpose: Documents the CLI (Click-based), HTTP health server, and observability API surfaces. Lists all CLI command groups (run, health, quarantine, checkpoint, run-manifest, export, maintenance, diagnostics) and their options.

pages.title: Medallion Data Pipeline
pages.purpose: Overview of the Bronze → Silver → Gold data flow, the write lifecycle for each layer, and how data quality is enforced at each stage. Links to child pages for each layer and for the Composite Pipeline pattern.

pages.title: Bronze Layer
pages.purpose: Details raw data ingestion: JSONL+zstd format, path conventions, metadata sidecars, atomic writes, BronzeWriter implementation, and the append-only immutability guarantee.

pages.title: Silver Layer
pages.purpose: Covers normalized Delta Lake tables: schema enforcement via PyArrow, Pandera validation, upsert/merge operations, schema drift detection, DQ metrics computation, SilverWriter write lifecycle, and metadata sidecars.

pages.title: Gold Layer
pages.purpose: Covers analysis-ready Gold tables: strict Pandera validation, write modes (overwrite, append, SCD2), dual-write/shadow-write rollout, GoldWriter pipeline, content-hash guard, and Gold schema contracts.

pages.title: Composite Pipeline Pattern
pages.purpose: Explains ADR-026: the Seed → Dependency → Enricher → Merge pattern for combining data from multiple providers. Covers MergeService, EnrichmentCoordinatorService, CompositePipelineState FSM, conflict resolution strategies, and checkpoint resumability.

pages.title: Data Schemas and Normalization
pages.purpose: Overview of the schema hierarchy (ETLRecordSchema → PublicationBaseSchema → provider schemas) and the normalization profile system. Links to child pages for Silver schemas, Gold contracts, and normalization profiles.

pages.title: Silver Schemas
pages.purpose: Documents all provider-specific Silver layer Pandera schemas: ETLRecordSchema base, PublicationBaseSchema, and provider schemas for ChEMBL, PubChem, UniProt, PubMed, OpenAlex, CrossRef, and SemanticScholar. Covers field conventions, DQ flags, and content hash.

pages.title: Gold Contracts
pages.purpose: Documents Gold layer Pandera contracts for unified entities (ChEMBLActivityGoldSchema, ChEMBLMoleculeGoldSchema, publication schemas). Explains schema unification across providers, the _lookup_method field, and contract versioning.

pages.title: Normalization Profiles
pages.purpose: Explains the normalization profile system: build_standard_profile factory, normalizer families (passthrough, json_string_strict, binary_flag, operator), pseudo-null handling, ChEMBL vocabulary enforcement, and the Pipeline Normalization Field Matrix report.

pages.title: Provider Adapters
pages.purpose: Overview of the adapter infrastructure: BaseHttpAdapter, BaseSyncAdapter, health/resilience patterns, and the list of supported providers. Links to child pages for each provider group.

pages.title: HTTP Client and Resilience
pages.purpose: Documents the UnifiedHTTPClient, circuit breaker (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN states), token-bucket rate limiter, retry mixin, and the ErrorService taxonomy. Explains how adapters share these cross-cutting concerns.

pages.title: ChEMBL Adapter
pages.purpose: Details the ChEMBL adapter: adaptive batch-size reduction on DEGRADED health, composite-key deduplication for unstable pagination, health probe, and the ChEMBL entity mapper. Covers activity, assay, molecule, target, publication, and cell-line entities.

pages.title: Publication Provider Adapters
pages.purpose: Documents adapters for PubMed (Entrez E-utilities, XML parsing, title fallback), OpenAlex (Polite Pool, cursor pagination, inverted-index reconstruction), CrossRef (DOI-centric, CrossRefQueryBuilder), and SemanticScholar (batch lookups, TLDR). Covers shared fallback orchestration.

pages.title: PubChem and UniProt Adapters
pages.purpose: Documents the PubChem adapter (pubchempy sync wrapper, fetch by SMILES/CID/name, BaseSyncAdapter thread-pool pattern) and the UniProt adapter (paginated protein/feature/sequence fetching, ID mapping client, idmapping_transformer).

pages.title: Pipeline Transformers
pages.purpose: Overview of the transformer architecture: BaseTransformer, extraction blocks/bundles pattern, entity inflation, Silver conversion, and the transformer dependency context. Links to child pages for publication and ChEMBL/bio-entity transformers.

pages.title: Publication Transformers
pages.purpose: Details transformers for PubMed (XML extraction blocks, MeSH terms, author parsing), OpenAlex (bundle pattern, inverted-index abstract, FWCI), CrossRef (DOI validation, Crossmark), SemanticScholar (TLDR, citation context), and ChEMBL publications. Covers PII hashing and content hash generation.

pages.title: ChEMBL and Bio-Entity Transformers
pages.purpose: Documents ChEMBL transformers for activity, assay, molecule, target, target-component, cell-line, and tissue. Covers the base ChEMBL transformer, FieldSpec/FieldGroup DSL, and UniProt/PubChem transformers.

pages.title: Configuration System
pages.purpose: Overview of the YAML-based configuration system: hierarchy (base → provider → entity), Pydantic validation, unified entity config format (ADR-039), and runtime resolution. Links to child pages for entity configs and pipeline config schema.

pages.title: Entity and Provider Configs
pages.purpose: Documents the unified entity YAML format: column_groups (system/business/dq), quality validations, SCD2 settings, filter rules, and composite pipeline configs. Covers all supported entities (ChEMBL activity/assay/molecule/target, UniProt protein, PubChem compound, publications).

pages.title: Pipeline Config Schema and Runtime Resolution
pages.purpose: Documents PipelineConfig Pydantic schema, config_loader merge strategy (ADR-037), inputs_runtime_helpers RuntimeConfig projection, filter config loader, and DQ config loader. Covers environment variable overrides and config snapshot testing.

pages.title: Observability and Operations
pages.purpose: Overview of the observability stack (Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry tracing, structlog logging) and operational tooling. Links to child pages for metrics/Grafana, the Run Control Plane, and the Quarantine subsystem.

pages.title: Repository Layout and Source Surfaces
pages.purpose: Maps the main repository surface families: src, docs, configs, tests, scripts, reports, grafana, and memory. Explains where to look first for runtime truth versus derived navigation.

pages.title: Supported Providers and Pipelines
pages.purpose: Summarises the provider catalog, the entity pipeline families, and where provider-specific configs and tests live. Orients readers around how provider coverage maps to runtime and validation surfaces.

page_notes.content: Canonical anchors: configs/entities/, configs/composites/, src/bioetl/infrastructure/adapters/, tests/fixtures/vcr/, tests/integration/.

pages.title: ADR Catalogue and Decision Flow
pages.purpose: Explains how ADRs are indexed, how superseded decisions are handled, and how to trace an architectural claim back to a maintained decision record.

pages.title: Documentation Governance and Drift
pages.purpose: Describes doc claim surfaces, freshness expectations, and the validation checks used to prevent documentation drift from accumulating.

pages.title: File Policy and Protected Surfaces
pages.purpose: Describes protected paths, machine-local surfaces, and file-policy rules that AI assistants must respect when editing the repository.

pages.title: Memory Workflow
pages.purpose: Explains the canonical pre-task and post-task memory loop, retrieval order, promotion rules, and how episodic versus curated memory should be used.
pages.parent: AI Runtime, Memory, and MCP Governance

pages.title: MCP Surfaces
pages.purpose: Lists the configured MCP clients and distinguishes local wrapper-based servers from remote HTTP MCP endpoints.
pages.parent: AI Runtime, Memory, and MCP Governance

pages.title: DeepWiki Navigation Strategy
pages.purpose: Describes how DeepWiki is used as a derived navigation layer for discovery, while canonical truth remains in docs, code, configs, tests, and accepted ADRs.

pages.title: Layer Boundaries and Import Rules
pages.purpose: Explains the layer separation rules and import boundaries that protect the domain from infrastructure leakage.

pages.title: Ports and Facades
pages.purpose: Shows how the domain port facade and adapter-facing APIs keep the public surface narrow and explicit.

pages.title: Dependency Injection and Wiring Rules
pages.purpose: Describes how composition wires interfaces, adapters, and application services without moving policy into runtime glue.

pages.title: Domain Ports
pages.purpose: Documents the Protocol and ABC interfaces that define the domain contract boundaries.

pages.title: Aggregates and Value Objects
pages.purpose: Explains the aggregate and value-object model, deterministic identity rules, and immutability expectations in the domain layer.

pages.title: Schemas and Exceptions
pages.purpose: Covers domain schemas, schema contracts, and the exception hierarchy used to signal invariant violations.

pages.title: Runner and Batch Flow
pages.purpose: Walks through pipeline execution from runner to batch executor and where orchestration stops before adapter logic begins.

pages.title: Record Processing
pages.purpose: Describes record-level processing, enrichment coordination, and how per-record policy stays separate from adapter implementations.

pages.title: Data Quality and Error Services
pages.purpose: Covers the data-quality service, validation hooks, and the error taxonomy used by application orchestration.

pages.title: Storage Writers and Checkpointing
pages.purpose: Explains Bronze/Silver/Gold writers, checkpoint persistence, and the storage boundary between application policy and infrastructure I/O.

pages.title: HTTP Client Resilience
pages.purpose: Documents retry, circuit breaker, rate limiting, and unified HTTP client behavior for adapters.

pages.title: Quarantine and Validation
pages.purpose: Covers quarantine persistence, validation guards, and how failed records are isolated without mutating the domain model.

pages.title: Bootstrap and Factory Wiring
pages.purpose: Describes the bootstrap assembly and factory entry points that turn canonical config into runnable services.

pages.title: Provider Registry and Runtime Builders
pages.purpose: Explains provider registry, runtime builders, and the way composition resolves provider-specific implementations.

pages.title: Runtime Diagnostics Entry Points
pages.purpose: Covers CLI diagnostics and maintenance commands that are not part of the pipeline runtime but are still governed surfaces.

pages.title: HTTP Health and Observability Surfaces
pages.purpose: Describes the health server, observability endpoints, and the contract between interface surfaces and monitoring tooling.

pages.title: Bronze Write Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Details the Bronze ingestion lifecycle, append-only guarantees, sidecar metadata, and atomic write semantics.

pages.title: Silver Merge and Upsert Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Explains Silver table normalization, merge/upsert behavior, drift checks, and row-level DQ signals.

pages.title: Gold Contracts and Rollout Strategy
pages.purpose: Covers Gold validation contracts, rollout modes, and the strict publishing rules for analysis-ready tables.

pages.title: Composite Seed and Dependency Phases
pages.purpose: Describes the seed and dependency phases of the composite pipeline pattern, including provider ordering and prerequisites.

pages.title: Composite Enricher and Merge Phases
pages.purpose: Explains the enricher and merge phases, conflict handling, and how composite state transitions preserve resumability.

pages.title: Schema Hierarchy and Contracts
pages.purpose: Shows how the schema hierarchy maps to provider-specific validation contracts and shared base schemas.

pages.title: Monitoring and Dashboards
pages.purpose: Covers dashboards, alerting surfaces, and the monitoring inventory used by operators.
